call_points.text: Music vertical revenue growth guided at 20-23% YoY for FY27, unchanged.
Annual music EBITDA margin guided at 60-65%, held despite higher content spend.
New music content spend for FY27 expected at ₹300-350 Cr, most already committed.
Content investment step-up to temper from FY28; 25-30% market share targeted.
Music vertical Q1 revenue ₹230.6 Cr, up 39% YoY, helped by a low base last year.
Video vertical revenue fell 52% to ~₹17 Cr as films business is wound down.
Other income fell as cash was diverted to Bhansali Productions.
Pocket Aces reached breakeven in FY26 and is expected to turn profitable this year.
60% of FY26 music revenue came from content released after 2000, 45% after 2020.
Analyst asked for organic vs acquired catalog split; management declined to separate the numbers.
From FY28, content investment to rise only at high single to low double-digit percentage annually, no more step jumps.
Music net margin expected to improve 300-500 bps over 3-5 years from the current 46-50% range.
FY26 content spend was ₹235 Cr on new music plus ₹105 Cr on catalogue purchases; spend was below plan as Love & War and Paradise were pushed to FY27.
Capital allocated to video and live verticals to fall from 18% of total to mid-single digits as film production is wound down.
Bhansali Productions minority investment secures A and B+ Hindi film music albums for the next 24-30 months at a pre-agreed formula.
Unallocable expenditure rose to ₹73 Cr in FY26 from ₹37 Cr in FY25, mainly because interest income fell as QIP funds were deployed.
Short-format video deals remain fixed-fee annual contracts, not ad-revenue share, which management calls a concern.
Management declined to share subscription revenue split, calling it competitor-sensitive; said free audio revenue is flat and growth comes from paid.
ROE at 13.3% is below management's satisfaction; QIP proceeds deployed into content, Pocket Aces and Bhansali, with ROE expected to rise.
